instruction.text: This picture shows a chicken’s life cycle. Select the correct stage in the chicken’s life.

feedback.correct: Chickens are domesticated birds. That means they have been changed by being kept by humans for a long time — usually for farming purposes. A chicken’s life span is between 5 and 10 years, depending on the breed, housing, care and food of the chicken.

Female chickens can lay either fertile or infertile eggs. Only the fertile eggs can hatch. The hen sits on the eggs and makes sure to keep them at a constant temperature. After 21 days of brooding, the baby chick hatches.
In this stage, the chicken is not yet an adult — similar to being a teenager. This stage lasts about 5 months. Then, the chicken reaches adulthood and the life cycle can start all over again.
